Great! I'm ready to help you create images with a diffusion model. Please provide the details you have in mind, such as the type of image, resolution, colors, or any specific elements you want to include in the image. Once you've provided these details, I'll do my best to guide you through the process.

A Prompt is a short text phrase that the Midjourney Bot interprets to produce an image. The Midjourney Bot breaks down the words and phrases in a prompt into smaller pieces, called tokens, that can be compared to its training data and then used to generate an image. A well-crafted prompt can help make unique and exciting images. Structure Basic Prompts A basic prompt can be as simple as a single word, phrase or emoji

Advanced Prompts More advanced prompts can include one or more image URLs, multiple text phrases, and one or more parameters

Image Prompts Image URLs can be added to a prompt to influence the style and content of the finished result. Image URLs always go at the front of a prompt. Read more about Image Prompts

Prompt Text The text description of what image you want to generate. See below for prompting information and tips. Well-written prompts help generate amazing images.

Parameters Parameters change how an image generates. Parameters can change aspect ratios, models, upscalers, and lots more. Parameters go at the end of the prompt. Read more about Parameters

Prompting Notes Prompt Length Prompts can be very simple. Single words (or even an emoji!) will produce an image. Very short prompts will rely heavily on Midjourney’s default style, so a more descriptive prompt is better for a unique look. However, super-long prompts aren’t always better. Concentrate on the main concepts you want to create.

Grammar The Midjourney Bot does not understand grammar, sentence structure, or words like humans. Word choice also matters. More specific synonyms work better in many circumstances. Instead of big, try gigantic, enormous, or immense. Remove words when possible. Fewer words mean each word has a more powerful influence. Use commas, brackets, and hyphens to help organize your thoughts, but know the Midjourney Bot will not reliably interpret them. The Midjourney Bot does not consider capitalization. Midjourney Model Version 4 is slightly better than other models at interpreting traditional sentence structure.

Focus on What you Want It is better to describe what you want instead of what you don’t want. If you ask for a party with “no cake,” your image will probably include a cake. If you want to ensure an object is not in the final image, try advance prompting using the --no parameter.

Think About What Details Matter Anything left unsaid may suprise you. Be as specific or vague as you want, but anything you leave out will be randomized. Being vague is a great way to get variety, but you may not get the specific details you want. Try to be clear about any context or details that are important to you. Think about:

Subject: person, animal, character, location, object, etc.

Medium: photo, painting, illustration, sculpture, doodle, tapestry, etc.

Environment: indoors, outdoors, on the moon, in Narnia, underwater, the Emerald City, etc.

Lighting: soft, ambient, overcast, neon, studio lights, etc

Color: vibrant, muted, bright, monochromatic, colorful, black and white, pastel, etc.

Mood: Sedate, calm, raucous, energetic, etc.

Composition: Portrait, headshot, closeup, birds-eye view, etc.

Use Collective Nouns Plural words leave a lot to chance. Try specific numbers. "Three cats" is more specific than "cats." Collective nouns also work, “flock of birds” instead of "birds.”

Midjourney routinely releases new model versions to improve efficiency, coherency, and quality. The latest model is the default, but other models can be used using the --version or --v parameter or by using the /settings command and selecting a model version. Different models excel at different types of images.

--version accepts the values 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. --version can be abbreviated --v

Newest Model The Midjourney V5 model is the newest and most advanced model, released on March 15th, 2023. To use this model, add the --v 5 parameter to the end of a prompt, or use the /settings command and select 5️⃣ MJ Version 5 This model has very high Coherency, excels at interpreting natural language prompts, is higher resolution, and supports advanced features like repeating patterns with --tile

Prompt: vibrant California poppies --v 5

Prompt: high contrast surreal collage --v 5

Current Model The Midjourney V4 model is an entirely new codebase and brand-new AI architecture designed by Midjourney and trained on the new Midjourney AI supercluster. The latest Midjourney model has more knowledge of creatures, places, objects, and more. It's much better at getting small details right and can handle complex prompts with multiple characters or objects. The Version 4 model supports advanced functionality like image prompting and multi-prompts. This model has very high Coherency and excels with Image Prompts.

Prompt: vibrant California poppies

Prompt: high contrast surreal collage

Version 4 Styles 4a, 4b, and 4c Midjourney Model Version 4 has three slightly different "flavors" with slight tweaks to the stylistic tuning of the model. Experiment with these versions by adding --style 4a, --style 4b, or --style 4c to the end of a V4 prompt. --v 4 --style 4c is the current default and does not need to be added to the end of a prompt.

Note on Style 4a and 4b

--style 4a and --style 4b only support 1:1, 2:3, and 3:2 aspect ratios. --style 4c support aspect ratios up to 1:2 or 2:1.

Test Models Occasionally new models are released temporarily for community testing and feedback. There are currently two available test models: --test and --testp, which can be combined with the --creative parameter for more varied compositions. prompt example: /imagine prompt vibrant California poppies --testp --creative

Test models only support --stylize values between 1250–5000. Test models do not support multi-prompts or image-prompts Test models have a maximum aspect ratio of 3:2 or 2:3. Test models only generate two initial grid images when the aspect ratio is 1:1. Test models only generate one initial grid image when the aspect ratio is not 1:1. Words near the front of the prompt may matter more than words near the back.

There are two modes for image generation, Fast Mode and Relax Mode. Fast Mode tries to give you a GPU instantly. It's the highest-priority processing tier and uses your subscription's monthly GPU time. Relax Mode queues your generation behind others based on how much you've used the system. Relax Mode wait times are variable and usually range from 1–10 minutes. By default, your images will be generated using Fast mode. You can switch to Relax if you have a Standard or Pro subscription.

Parameters are options added to a prompt that change how an image generates. Parameters can change an image's Aspect Ratios, switch between Midjourney Model Versions, change which Upscaler is used, and lots more. Parameters are always added to the end of a prompt. You can add multiple parameters to each prompt.

Using an Apple device?

Many apple devices automatically change double hyphens (--) to an em-dash (—). Midjourney accepts both!

Basic Parameters Aspect Ratios --aspect, or --ar Change the aspect ratio of a generation. Chaos --chaos Change how varied the results will be. Higher values produce more unusual and unexpected generations. No --no Negative prompting, --no plants would try to remove plants from the image. Quality --quality <.25, .5, 1, or 2>, or --q <.25, .5, 1, or 2> How much rendering quality time you want to spend. The default value is 1. Higher values cost more and lower values cost less. Seed --seed The Midjourney bot uses a seed number to create a field of visual noise, like television static, as a starting point to generate the initial image grids. Seed numbers are generated randomly for each image but can be specified with the --seed or --sameseed parameter. Using the same seed number and prompt will produce similar ending images. Stop --stop Use the --stop parameter to finish a Job partway through the process. Stopping a Job at an earlier percentage can create blurrier, less detailed results. Style --style <4a, 4b or 4c> Switch between versions of the Midjourney Model Version 4 Stylize --stylize , or --s parameter influences how strongly Midjourney's default aesthetic style is applied to Jobs. Uplight --uplight Use an alternative "light" upscaler when selecting the U buttons. The results are closer to the original grid image. The upscaled image is less detailed and smoother. Upbeta --upbeta Use an alternative beta upscaler when selecting the U buttons. The results are closer to the original grid image. The upscaled image has significantly fewer added details. Aspect Ratios

The --aspect or --ar parameter changes the aspect ratio of the generated image. An aspect ratio is the width-to-height ratio of an image. It is typically expressed as two numbers separated by a colon, such as 7:4 or 4:3. A square image has equal width and height, described as a 1:1 aspect ratio. The image could be 1000px × 1000px, or 1500px × 1500px, and the aspect ratio would still be 1:1. A computer screen might have a ratio of 16:10. The width is 1.6 times longer than the height. So the image could be 1600px × 1000px, 4000px × 2000px, 320px x 200px, etc.

The default aspect ratio is 1:1. --aspect must use whole numbers. Use 139:100 instead of 1.39:1. The aspect ratio impacts the shape and composition of a generated image. Some aspect ratios may be slightly changed when upscaling.

Max Aspect Ratios Different Midjourney Version Models have different maximum aspect ratios.

Version 5 Version 4c (default) Version 4a or 4b Version 3 Test / Testp niji

Ratios any\* 1:2 to 2:1 Only: 1:1, 2:3 or 3:2 5:2 to2:5 3:2 to 2:3 1:2 to 2:1

The --ar parameter will accept any aspect ratio from 1:1 (square) up to the maximum aspect ratio for each model. However, final outputs may be slightly modified during image generation or upscaling. Example: prompts using --ar 16:9 (1.78) create images with a 7:4 (1.75) aspect ratio. \* Aspect ratios greater than 2:1 are experimental and may produce unpredicatble results.

prompt example: imagine/ prompt vibrant california poppies --ar 5:4

Common Midjourney Aspect Ratios --aspect 1:1 Default aspect ratio. --aspect 5:4 Common frame and print ratio. --aspect 3:2 Common in print photography. --aspect 7:4 Close to HD TV screens and smartphone screens.

How to Change the Aspect Ratio Use Aspect Ratio Parameters Add --aspect :, or --ar : to the end of your prompt.

Chaos

The --chaos or --c parameter influences how varied the initial image grids are. High --chaos values will produce more unusual and unexpected results and compositions. Lower --chaos values have more reliable, repeatable results.

--chaos accepts values 0–100. The default --chaos value is 0.

The Influence of Chaos on Jobs Low --chaos values Using a low --chaos value, or not specifying a value, will produce initial image grids that are slightly varied each time a Job is run. prompt example: imagine/ prompt watermelon owl hybrid

High --chaos Values Using a higher --chaos value will produce initial image grids that are more varied and unexpected each time a Job is run. prompt example: imagine/ prompt watermelon owl hybrid --c 50

Very High --chaos Values Using extremely high --chaos values will produce initial image grids that are varied and have unexpected compositions or artistic mediums each time a Job is run. prompt example: imagine/ prompt watermelon owl hybrid --c 100

How to Change the Chaos Value Use the --chaos or --c Parameter Add --chaos or --c to the end of your prompt.

Quality

The --quality or --q parameter changes how much time is spent generating an image. Higher-quality settings take longer to process and produce more details. Higher values also mean more GPU minutes are used per job. The quality setting does not impact resolution.

The default --quality value is 1. Higher values use more of your subscription's GPU minutes. --quality accepts the values: .25, .5, and 1 for the default model. Larger values will be rounded down to 1. --quality only influences the initial image generation. --quality works with Model Versions 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and niji.

Quality Settings Higher --quality settings aren't always better. Sometimes a lower --quality settings can produce better results—depending on the image you're trying to create. Lower --quality settings might be best for a gestural abstract look. Higher --quality values may improve the look of architectural images that benefit from many details. Choose the setting that best matches the kind of image you're hoping to create. Prompt example: /imagine prompt woodcut birch forest --q .25 Version 4

The Midjourney Bot processes jobs on high-end GPUs. Each minute that it takes to complete a job is a GPU minute. You have a limited amount of GPU minutes when in Fast Mode. Because image generations may be processed on multiple GPUs simultaneously, GPU minutes are not directly connected to the time you wait for an image to generate.

Seeds
The Midjourney bot uses a seed number to create a field of visual noise, like television static, as a starting point to generate the initial image grids. Seed numbers are generated randomly for each image but can be specified with the --seed or --sameseed parameter. Using the same seed number and prompt will produce similar ending images.

--seed accepts whole numbers 0–4294967295. --seed values only influence the initial image grid. --seed values Model Versions 1, 2, 3, test, and testp are non-deterministic and will produce similar, not identical, images. Using the same prompt+seed+parameters in Model Versions 4, 5 and niji will produce identical images.

Seed Parameter If no Seed is specified, Midjourney will use a randomly generated seed number, producing a wide variety of options each time a prompt is used.

Jobs run three times with random seeds: prompt example: /imagine prompt celadon owl pitcher

Jobs run two times with --seed 123: prompt example: /imagine prompt celadon owl pitcher --seed 123

Sameseed Parameter --seed values create a single large random noise field applied across all images in the initial grid. When --sameseed is specified, all images in the initial grid use the same starting noise and will produce very similar generated images.

--sameseed accepts whole numbers 0–4294967295. --sameseed is only compatible with Model Versions 1, 2, 3, test, and testp.

Stylize
This Midjourney Bot has been trained to produce images that favor artistic color, composition, and forms. The --stylize or --s parameter influences how strongly this training is applied. Low stylization values produce images that closely match the prompt but are less artistic. High stylization values create images that are very artistic but less connected to the prompt.

--stylize's default value is 100 and accepts integer values 0–1000 when using the default [V4 model].

Tile

The --tile parameter generates images that can be used as repeating tiles to create seamless patterns for fabrics, wallpapers and textures.

--tile works with Model Versions 1, 2, 3 and 5. --tile only generates a single tile. Use a pattern making tool like this Seamless Pattern Checker to see the tile repeat.

Tile Examples Using Midjourney Model Test/Testp

prompt torn cardboard roses --testp --tile

apakah kamu mengenal Buya Hamka, salah satu tokoh Muhammadiyah juga ya?

Buya Hamka atau Haji Abdul Malik Karim Amrullah adalah seorang ulama, sastrawan, dan cendekiawan Muslim yang lahir pada 17 Februari 1908 di Minangkabau, Sumatera Barat. Apakah kamu tahu tentang cerita Buya Hamka dipenjara? Seperti apa detail ceritanya

apakah kamu kenal Presiden Jenderal Soeharto? bagaimana hubungan beliau dengan para tokoh Dakwah Islam Indonesia dan ada peran beliau terhadap Dakwah Islam di Indonesia ?

Ya, saya mengenal Presiden Jenderal Soeharto, yang merupakan Presiden kedua Republik Indonesia. Beliau menjabat selama 32 tahun, dari tahun 1967 hingga 1998, dalam era yang dikenal sebagai Orde Baru. Jenderal Soeharto adalah seorang tokoh militer yang naik ke tampuk kekuasaan setelah peristiwa G30S/PKI pada tahun 1965 dan menggantikan Presiden Soekarno.

Hubungan antara Presiden Jenderal Soeharto dengan para tokoh dakwah Islam Indonesia cukup kompleks. Pada awal pemerintahannya, Soeharto menghadapi situasi politik yang tidak stabil dan perlu mendapatkan dukungan dari berbagai pihak, termasuk kelompok agama. Oleh karena itu, Soeharto mulai menjalin hubungan dengan para tokoh agama Islam, termasuk tokoh-tokoh Muhammadiyah dan Nahdlatul Ulama (NU).

Selama pemerintahannya, Presiden Jenderal Soeharto memiliki beberapa peran yang berdampak pada dakwah Islam di Indonesia, di antaranya:

Organisasi ini dianggap sebagai salah satu upaya Soeharto untuk mendekatkan diri dengan kalangan Islam.

3. Pembangunan infrastruktur keagamaan: Pemerintahan Soeharto juga mendukung pembangunan infrastruktur keagamaan, seperti masjid, madrasah, dan pondok pesantren, untuk memperkuat dakwah Islam di Indonesia.

Namun, hubungan antara Soeharto dan para tokoh dakwah Islam Indonesia tidak selalu harmonis. Soeharto dikenal memiliki kebijakan yang represif terhadap kelompok-kelompok yang dianggap sebagai ancaman terhadap stabilitas politik, termasuk beberapa tokoh dan kelompok Islam. Misalnya, partai Masyumi, yang merupakan partai Islam, dilarang pada tahun 1960-an, dan beberapa tokoh Islam seperti Buya Hamka pernah mengalami penahanan karena dianggap terlibat dalam peristiwa G30S/PKI.

Secara keseluruhan, Presiden Jenderal Soeharto memiliki peran yang cukup signifikan dalam dakwah Islam di Indonesia, baik dalam hal pendukung maupun represif. Hubungannya dengan para tokoh dakwah Islam Indonesia sering kali dipengaruhi oleh dinamika politik dan kepentingan pemerintahan pada waktu itu.

kenapa di Indonesia Pancasila seakan akan di posisikan berlawanan dengan Dakwah Islam, atau seakan2 jika mengambil posisi politik Islam maka anti Pancasila? bagaimana perdapatmu? gunakan tabel komparasi jika diperlukan

Sebenarnya, di Indonesia Pancasila dan Dakwah Islam tidak seharusnya saling berlawanan. Pancasila sebagai dasar negara dan ideologi Indonesia, memiliki prinsip-prinsip yang sejalan dengan nilai-nilai yang diajarkan oleh agama Islam. Namun, dalam praktiknya, muncul beberapa persepsi yang menyebabkan seakan-akan Pancasila dan Dakwah Islam berlawanan. Berikut adalah beberapa alasan yang mungkin melatarbelakangi persepsi tersebut:

1. Sejarah perumusan Pancasila: Pada masa perumusan Pancasila, terjadi perdebatan antara kelompok yang mendukung prinsip "Islam sebagai dasar negara" dan kelompok yang ingin menciptakan negara yang inklusif dan pluralis. Akhirnya, prinsip "Ketuhanan Yang Maha Esa" yang diadopsi dalam Pancasila, mencerminkan kompromi antara kedua kelompok. Hal ini kadang-kadang dianggap sebagai penolakan terhadap prinsip politik Islam, meskipun sebenarnya Pancasila mengakomodasi nilai-nilai agama, termasuk Islam.
2. Politik Orde Baru: Pada masa pemerintahan Presiden Soeharto, ada kebijakan represif terhadap kelompok-kelompok politik yang dianggap mengancam stabilitas negara, termasuk beberapa kelompok politik Islam. Hal ini mungkin mempengaruhi persepsi tentang hubungan antara Pancasila dan Dakwah Islam.
3. Sikap pemerintah terhadap kelompok Islam: Terkadang, ada sikap yang cenderung mengkotak-kotakkan kelompok-kelompok politik dan agama di Indonesia. Kelompok yang dianggap mengusung politik Islam mungkin dianggap tidak sejalan dengan Pancasila, padahal kenyataannya, banyak nilai-nilai yang diajarkan oleh agama Islam sejalan dengan Pancasila.

Berikut tabel komparasi antara Pancasila dan Dakwah Islam:

| Pancasila | Dakwah Islam |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Ketuhanan Yang Maha Esa | 1. Tauhid |
| 2. Kemanusiaan yang adil dan beradab | 2. Adil dan beradab dalam hubungan antarmanusia |
| 3. Persatuan Indonesia | 3. Persaudaraan dan kesatuan umat |
| 4. Kerakyatan yang dipimpin oleh hikmat kebijaksanaan dalam permusyawaratan/perwakilan | 4. Syura (musyawarah) dalam pengambilan keputusan |
| 5. Keadilan sosial bagi seluruh rakyat Indonesia | 5. Keadilan sosial dan ekonomi |

Sebagai catatan, perbedaan-perbedaan yang ada antara Pancasila dan Dakwah Islam sebenarnya lebih pada interpretasi dan praktik politik, bukan pada prinsip-prinsip dasarnya. Dalam konteks Indonesia, Pancasila dan Dakwah Islam seharusnya bisa saling melengkapi dan mendukung satu sama lain dalam menciptakan negara yang adil, makmur, dan sejahtera.
apa bentuk logical fallacy dan bagaimana cara mengcounternya dari perspektif bahwa kalo Pancasilais maka tidak boleh atau bahkan anti islam politik?

Bentuk logical fallacy yang terdapat dalam pernyataan bahwa jika seseorang adalah Pancasilais, maka mereka tidak boleh atau bahkan anti-Islam politik, adalah "false dilemma" atau "false dichotomy." False dilemma adalah kesalahan logika yang terjadi ketika seseorang menghadapi dua pilihan yang seolah-olah eksklusif dan saling bertentangan, padahal sebenarnya ada pilihan atau solusi lain yang tidak dipertimbangkan.

Dalam konteks ini, false dilemma muncul ketika seseorang menganggap bahwa Pancasila dan Islam politik tidak bisa bersanding atau saling melengkapi, dan mereka harus memilih antara satu atau yang lain. Padahal, kenyataannya, Pancasila sebagai dasar negara Indonesia mengakomodasi nilai-nilai yang diajarkan oleh agama Islam, dan seharusnya bisa saling melengkapi dengan kepentingan-kepentingan politik yang mendasarkan diri pada ajaran Islam.

Untuk mengcounter argumen yang mengandung false dilemma ini, kita bisa melakukan beberapa hal berikut:

1. Tunjukkan bahwa Pancasila dan Islam politik memiliki kesamaan nilai-nilai dasar, seperti yang telah dijelaskan dalam tabel komparasi sebelumnya. Keduanya sejalan dalam banyak aspek, seperti ketuhanan, kemanusiaan, persatuan, demokrasi, dan keadilan sosial.
2. Berikan contoh bahwa ada banyak negara yang menganut sistem demokrasi yang mengakomodasi kepentingan agama, termasuk Islam, dalam politik dan tata kelola negara, tanpa harus mengorbankan prinsip-prinsip dasar seperti persatuan dan toleransi.
3. Jelaskan bahwa banyak tokoh dan organisasi Islam di Indonesia yang aktif dalam politik, tetapi tetap menjunjung tinggi nilai-nilai Pancasila dan konstitusi negara. Perjuangan dakwah Islam melalui jalur politik dan non-politik memiliki beberapa perbedaan esensial dalam metode, fokus, dan tujuan. Berikut ini perbedaan antara kedua jalur tersebut:

1. Metode:
* Jalur politik: Melibatkan partisipasi dalam proses politik formal, seperti pemilihan umum, pembentukan partai politik, pembuatan kebijakan publik, dan pengambilan posisi di pemerintahan atau parlemen. Contohnya, PKS yang aktif dalam politik, berpartisipasi dalam pemilu, dan mengusung calon anggota legislatif dan eksekutif.
* Jalur non-politik: Fokus pada kegiatan sosial, pendidikan, dakwah, dan kesejahteraan masyarakat yang tidak secara langsung terkait dengan proses politik formal. Contohnya, organisasi seperti Muhammadiyah dan Nahdlatul Ulama yang aktif dalam pendidikan, kesehatan, dan pemberdayaan masyarakat, meskipun mereka juga memiliki sayap politik.
1. Fokus:
* Jalur politik: Menciptakan perubahan sosial melalui pengaruh dalam sistem politik dan kebijakan publik. Misalnya, PKS di politik mungkin berfokus pada pencalonan anggota legislatif dan eksekutif yang akan mewakili kepentingan umat Islam dan membawa perubahan melalui undang-undang dan kebijakan.
* Jalur non-politik: Menciptakan perubahan sosial melalui pendidikan, peningkatan kualitas hidup masyarakat, dan dakwah langsung. Misalnya, PKS yang tidak aktif di politik mungkin lebih fokus pada kegiatan sosial, seperti pembangunan masjid, sekolah, dan rumah sakit.
1. Tujuan:
* Jalur politik: Tujuannya adalah untuk mempengaruhi kebijakan publik dan menghadirkan perwakilan umat Islam dalam sistem politik, serta mempromosikan nilai-nilai Islam dalam kehidupan berbangsa dan bernegara.
* Jalur non-politik: Tujuannya adalah untuk menyebarkan ajaran Islam, meningkatkan kualitas hidup umat Islam, dan memperkuat umat Islam melalui pendidikan, dakwah, dan pemberdayaan masyarakat.

Meskipun jalur politik dan non-politik memiliki perbedaan esensial dalam metode, fokus, dan tujuan, keduanya memiliki peran penting dalam perjuangan dakwah Islam di Indonesia. bagaimana detail taktis, teknis dan etis dalam penggunaan sumber daya negara untuk kepentingan partai dan anggotanya?

Penggunaan sumber daya negara untuk kepentingan partai dan anggotanya memang perlu dilakukan dengan cara yang adil, transparan, dan akuntabel, serta selalu mengedepankan kepentingan rakyat. Berikut adalah beberapa langkah taktis, teknis, dan etis yang dapat diambil:

1. Kepatuhan terhadap hukum: Pastikan bahwa semua kegiatan yang melibatkan penggunaan sumber daya negara selalu mematuhi hukum dan peraturan yang berlaku. Tidak ada penyalahgunaan kekuasaan atau korupsi dalam proses alokasi dan penggunaan sumber daya tersebut.
2. Transparansi: Tingkatkan transparansi dalam pengelolaan sumber daya negara dengan menyediakan informasi yang jelas dan mudah diakses mengenai penggunaan dan alokasi sumber daya tersebut. Informasi ini harus disampaikan kepada publik melalui laporan keuangan, situs web, dan media lainnya.
3. Akuntabilitas: Tetapkan sistem pengawasan yang efektif untuk memastikan bahwa penggunaan sumber daya negara sesuai dengan tujuan yang telah ditetapkan. Pengawasan ini dapat melibatkan lembaga pengawas internal partai, lembaga pengawas eksternal (seperti KPK dan BPK), serta masyarakat.
4. Partisipasi: Libatkan konstituen, anggota, dan masyarakat dalam proses pengambilan keputusan yang berkaitan dengan penggunaan sumber daya negara. Hal ini dapat dilakukan melalui konsultasi publik, forum diskusi, dan mekanisme partisipatif lainnya.
5. Prioritaskan kepentingan rakyat: Pastikan bahwa penggunaan sumber daya negara selalu mengedepankan kepentingan rakyat, terutama dalam hal peningkatan kualitas hidup, pendidikan, kesehatan, dan infrastruktur. Setiap kebijakan dan program yang dijalankan harus memberikan manfaat langsung kepada masyarakat.
6. Pendidikan dan pelatihan: Berikan pendidikan dan pelatihan kepada anggota partai tentang etika penggunaan sumber daya negara, termasuk pentingnya integritas, kejujuran, dan tanggung jawab dalam pengelolaan sumber daya tersebut.
7. Evaluasi dan perbaikan: Lakukan evaluasi secara berkala terhadap penggunaan sumber daya negara dan implementasikan perbaikan yang diperlukan untuk meningkatkan efisiensi, efektivitas, dan keadilan dalam pengelolaannya.

Dengan mengikuti langkah-langkah ini, partai politik seperti PKS dapat memastikan bahwa penggunaan sumber daya negara dilakukan dengan cara yang adil, transparan, dan akuntabel, serta selalu mengedepankan kepentingan rakyat sebagai prioritas utama.

strategi seperti apa yang paling efektif untuk meningkatkan kesejahteraan partai dan anggotanya melalui kekuasaan?

Fokus pada kebijakan yang pro-rakyat: Kembangkan dan dukung kebijakan yang secara langsung memberikan manfaat kepada masyarakat, seperti peningkatan akses pendidikan, kesehatan, perumahan, dan infrastruktur. 2. Pendidikan dan pelatihan anggota partai: Berinvestasi dalam pengembangan kapasitas anggota partai melalui pendidikan, pelatihan, dan pengembangan kepemimpinan. Hal ini akan membantu anggota partai untuk lebih efektif dalam menjalankan tugas dan tanggung jawab mereka, serta memajukan kesejahteraan mereka secara individu.
3. Kepemimpinan yang etis dan transparan: Tingkatkan integritas dan akuntabilitas partai dengan memastikan bahwa semua anggota partai, terutama pemimpin, menjalankan tugas mereka dengan cara yang etis, transparan, dan bertanggung jawab. Kepemimpinan yang baik akan meningkatkan kepercayaan publik dan mempengaruhi kesejahteraan partai dan anggotanya.
4. Pengelolaan sumber daya partai yang efisien: Kelola sumber daya partai, termasuk dana, sumber daya manusia, dan infrastruktur, dengan cara yang efisien dan efektif. Hal ini akan memastikan bahwa partai dapat memaksimalkan potensi sumber daya yang dimilikinya untuk mencapai tujuan dan meningkatkan kesejahteraan anggotanya.
5. Jalin hubungan dan kolaborasi dengan berbagai pihak: Bangun hubungan yang kuat dengan berbagai kelompok masyarakat, sektor swasta, LSM, dan partai politik lain. Kolaborasi ini akan membantu partai dalam mencapai tujuan bersama dan memperkuat posisi partai dalam sistem politik.
6. Inovasi dan adaptasi: Kembangkan inovasi dalam kebijakan, program, dan metode kerja partai untuk lebih efektif dalam menjawab tantangan yang dihadapi masyarakat dan anggota partai. Adaptasi yang cepat terhadap perubahan situasi dan kebutuhan akan meningkatkan kinerja partai dan kesejahteraan anggotanya.

Dengan mengikuti langkah strategis ini, PKS atau partai politik lain dapat meningkatkan kesejahteraan partai dan anggotanya melalui kekuasaan dengan cara yang etis, inklusif, dan berkelanjutan. transform_data <- function(data, products_list) {
```R
  # Create an empty data frame to store the transformed data
  transformed_data <- data.frame()

  # Iterate through each row in the original data frame
  for (i in 1:nrow(data)) {
    # Extract user-specific information
```

 question <- as.integer(gsub("CHOICE\_", "", choice\_col))
 
 # Get the product index for Tarjeta A and Tarjeta B

 # Make sure the index is within the bounds of the products\_list
 if (chosen\_product\_index >= 1 && chosen\_product\_index <= length(products\_list)) {

It's crucial to examine the assumptions of the linear regression model and perform diagnostics to ensure that the model is appropriate for the data. You can also consider trying other models and comparing their performance to find the best model for your data.

"The Devil's Den" follows the lives of five teenagers - each with a unique and troubled background - who find themselves at the notorious Los Padrinos Juvenile Hall. As they struggle to come to terms with their past mistakes and forge a path towards redemption, they begin to experience inexplicable supernatural occurrences within the facility.

To cope with the supernatural events and find answers, the teens form an unlikely alliance and take it upon themselves to solve a new mystery each episode. These episodic mysteries, ranging from ghostly apparitions to bizarre phenomena, push the teens to work together and use their individual skills to uncover the truth. As they solve each case, they unravel clues that point to a larger, overarching mystery connected to the haunting of the Devil's Den and their own personal stories.

Through their shared experiences, the group will grow and learn the value of friendship, trust, and redemption as they work to uncover the mysteries of the Devil's Den.

Main Characters:

1. Alex - The troubled female leader, haunted by a family tragedy.
2. Jasmine - A rebellious, street-smart girl with a hidden vulnerable side.
3. Pretzel - A tech-savvy introvert who uses his intelligence to help solve the mystery.
4. Heather - A gifted artist whose creativity allows her to see beyond the ordinary.
5. Carlos - A former gang member seeking a second chance at life, returning to Los Padrinos after a stay at a different juvenile facility during its closure and rehabilitation.

Setting: Los Padrinos Juvenile Hall (Devil's Den) - Downey, California.

The new management of the facility appears to be more caring, progressive, and aware of its responsibility. However, beneath the surface, a subtle underlying darkness persists, possibly contained within the walls themselves. This darkness and the facility's haunted reputation are known to Carlos, who shares his first-hand experiences with the rest of the group.

IoT Security Workshop: Video Interception
1
IoT Security - Video Interception
Background
This IoT experiment demonstrates the vulnerability in video image streaming when associated with a
local Access Point. Unlike the other IoT lab experiments we do not need to gain access to the Access
Point ID/password but rather we scan the frequency spectrum to find a channel in which video images
are being transmitted. We are not intercepting or altering these images – merely copying them out
using a set of IoT analysis tools.
In this experiment the video images are not encrypted – which is very commonly the case in practice! If
these images were encrypted then this adds another layer of analysis which has parallels to some of the
other experiments. The fact that TCP/IP data can be pulled out of a discovered frequency channel – as
used by all Access Points is quite alarming.
This experiment is carried out with some simple and inexpensive tools – Virtual Machines, an Alfa or
WiPi USB adaptor, server for the video images, Access Point, switch or hub and an IP camera – all for a
few hundred dollars. Thus the quality of what we will extract – particularly with respect to the pixels is
limited, but it does illustrate what could be done to an IoT video network with more expensive tools.
Configuration

Summary of key issues in this IoT video interception workshop
(i) There is no wired connection and no wireless connection for layer 3 and above (IP/TCP/UDP)
and thus no TCP segment repeat in the face of error.
(ii) It is necessary to force the lowest speed possible – therefore it is best to configure 802.11b in
preference to 802.11g/a/n in the Access Point
(iii) It is necessary to carry out some sort of frequency spectrum analysis to find out in which
frequency band we need to look for these TCP segments. For example possible frequency
bands are: 2.417GHz (Ch 2), 2.437GHz (Ch 6), 2.457GHz (Ch 10). airodump-ng on the
appropriate wireless channel can be used to assist with this as well.
(iv) It is necessary to experiment with different wireless channels – in particular 2, 6 and 10 in
order to find a ping injection test with 100% success rate. This will involve removing
interfering devices as far as possible. Other Access Points in the vicinity can cause problems.

AWUS036H 802.11b/g Long-Range Wireless USB Adapter or the WiPi adaptor.

Part 2
In this part we will use mitmproxy (man-in-the-middle proxy) from the Kali VM to intercept/modify
the IoT commands between the Android and Wifi T – essentially a transparent http proxy process.
When a transparent proxy is used, the connection is redirected into a proxy at the network layer,
without any client configuration being required. This makes transparent proxying ideal for those
situations where you cannot change client behaviour - proxy-oblivious Android applications being a
common example.
To achieve this, we need to introduce two extra components. The first is a redirection mechanism
that transparently reroutes a TCP connection destined for a server to a listening proxy server. This
usually takes the form of a firewall on the same host as the proxy server - iptables on Linux. Once the
client has initiated the connection, it makes a vanilla HTTP request, which might look something like
this:
GET /index.html HTTP/1.1
Note that this request differs from the explicit proxy variation, in that it omits the scheme and
hostname. How, then, do we know which upstream host to forward the request to? The routing
mechanism that has performed the redirection keeps track of the original destination for us. Each
routing mechanism has a different way of exposing this data, so this introduces the second
component required for working transparent proxying: a host module that knows how to retrieve
the original destination address from the router. In mitmproxy, this takes the form of a built-in set of
modules that know how to talk to each platform’s redirection mechanism.

change it or cancel hold. When HOLD is turned off the thermostat will follow a weekly schedule.

IoT Switches:
TCP/IP interception and manipulation
This lab is designed to demonstrate how TCP-based connection can be intercepted and manipulated
in an IoT environment. This is an example of a commercial product which operates with TCP while
other labs in the section will demonstrate similar concepts with UDP connections.
There are two important tools for use in TCP interception: Mallory and mitmproxy. For this lab we
will use Mallory – as it has been used in other labs to demonstrate how ID/passwords can be
extracted from encrypted connections. In the second part of this experiment (Wifi Thermostat) we
will use mitmproxy to demonstrate interception and injection.
Although many of these devices are designed to work out of Cloud Services, in this case we will use a
Wifi lab and avoid complicated connections outside the lab. These connections to Cloud Services can
become complicated as firewalls in Universities and business are frequently configured to block
outgoing/incoming connections thus disabling the ability to carry out such experiments.
In the WeMo Switch to be used here actual connections to the Cloud Services requires firewall
traversal which for outgoing connections is not usually a problem but for incoming connections the
STUN (Session Traversal Utilities for NAT) protocol has to be used. This is a common problem for
example where IP phones behind a firewall need to operate with a VoIP provider in the Cloud.
The trace below shown the Belkin cloud service (54.82.106.255) attempting a TCP connection back
through the firewall to the router (192.168.1.64) and the subsequent dialogue.

its own Wifi hotspot, a DHCP server and the Mallory interception engine.

Outlook Command-Line Switches:

1. `/a <file>`: Creates a new message with the specified file attached.

3. `/c <itemtype>`: Creates a new item of the specified type, such as `ipm.note` for a new email or `ipm.appointment` for a new appointment.
4. `/checkclient`: Starts Outlook and checks for the default email client.
5. `/cleanserverrules`: Starts Outlook and deletes client- and server-based rules.
6. `/cleanviews`: Starts Outlook and deletes custom views.
7. `/embedding`: Starts Outlook without displaying the main Outlook window (used when Outlook is called by another application).
8. `/f <file>`: Opens the specified message file or .msg file.
9. `/hol <file>`: Imports the specified iCalendar .hol file.
10. `/ical <file>`: Imports the specified iCalendar .ics file.
11. `/importprf <file>`: Launches Outlook and imports the .prf file, which contains profile settings.
12. `/launchtraininghelp`: Displays Outlook's on-screen training.
13. `/m <mailto>`: Creates a new message with the specified email address in the To field.
14. `/nopreview`: Starts Outlook with the Reading Pane off.
15. `/pim <profilename>`: Opens Outlook with the specified profile or creates a new one if it doesn't exist.
16. `/profiles`: Opens Outlook and prompts the user to select a profile.
17. `/recycle`: Starts Outlook using an existing Outlook window, if available.
18. `/resetfolders`: Starts Outlook and resets folder names to their default names.
19. `/resetnavpane`: Starts Outlook and resets the Navigation Pane.
20. `/restore`: Starts Outlook with the Reading Pane minimized.
21. `/rpcdiag`: Opens Outlook and displays the remote procedure call (RPC) dialog box.
22. `/s <file>`: Opens the specified .pst file.
23. `/safe`: Starts Outlook in Safe Mode.
24. `/select <foldername>`: Opens Outlook and selects the specified folder.
25. `/share <path>`: Opens Outlook and shares the specified folder.
26. `/sniff`: Starts Outlook and forces a Send/Receive operation for all accounts.
27. `/t <file>`: Opens the specified .msg file as a task.

```python
import os
import glob
import datetime
from PIL import Image

def get_images_created_in_last_hour(folder):
    now = datetime.datetime.now()
    one_hour_ago = now - datetime.timedelta(hours=1)
    images = []
    for ext in ['*.png', '*.jpg', '*.jpeg']:
        pattern = os.path.join(folder, ext)
        for img_path in glob.glob(pattern):
            img_mtime = os.path.getmtime(img_path)
            img_datetime = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(img_mtime)
            if img_datetime > one_hour_ago:
                images.append(img_path)
    return images

def combine_images(images, max_width, padding):
    img_objects = [Image.open(img) for img in images]
    widths, heights = zip(*(img.size for img in img_objects))

    combined_width = min(sum(widths) + padding * (len(images) - 1), max_width)
    combined_height = sum(heights) + padding * (len(images) - 1)

    combined_image = Image.new('RGB', (combined_width, combined_height), color='white')

    x_offset = 0
    y_offset = 0

    for img in img_objects:
        combined_image.paste(img, (x_offset, y_offset))
        x_offset += img.size[0] + padding

        if x_offset + img.size[0] > max_width:
            x_offset = 0
            y_offset += img.size[1] + padding

    return combined_image

downloads_folder = os.path.expanduser("~/Downloads")
images = get_images_created_in_last_hour(downloads_folder)

if images:
    max_width = 1920  # Change this value to the desired screen width
    padding = int(5 * 0.03937 * 300)  # 5mm in pixels (assuming 300 DPI)
    combined_image = combine_images(images, max_width, padding)
    combined_image.save(os.path.join(downloads_folder, "combined_image.png"))
    print("Combined image saved as 'combined_image.png' in the Downloads folder.")
else:
    print("No images created in the last hour found.")
```

```python
import os

from PIL import Image
```

```python
def combine_images(images, max_width):
    images_per_row = math.ceil(math.sqrt(len(images)))
    padding = 5
    total_width = min(max_width, images_per_row * max(images, key=lambda img: img.width).width + (images_per_row - 1) * padding)
    rows = math.ceil(len(images) / images_per_row)
    max_height = rows * max(images, key=lambda img: img.height).height + (rows - 1) * padding

    combined_image = Image.new('RGB', (total_width, max_height), (255, 255, 255))

    x_offset = 0
    y_offset = 0
    row_height = 0

    for i, img in enumerate(images):
        if x_offset + img.width > max_width:
            x_offset = 0
            y_offset += row_height + padding
            row_height = 0

        combined_image.paste(img, (x_offset, y_offset))
        x_offset += img.width + padding
        row_height = max(row_height, img.height)

        if (i + 1) % images_per_row == 0:
            x_offset = 0
            y_offset += row_height + padding
            row_height = 0
```

Write description of every biaser used in a quiz

1. Confirmation Bias: Confirmation bias is the tendency to search for, interpret, favor, and recall information in a way that confirms one's preexisting beliefs or hypotheses. People tend to unconsciously ignore or undervalue information that contradicts their beliefs and give more weight to information that supports their views.
2. Anchoring Bias: Anchoring bias occurs when individuals rely too heavily on an initial piece of information (the "anchor") when making decisions. This can lead to insufficient adjustments based on new information, as people may give too much importance to the anchor and not properly consider other relevant factors.
3. Availability Heuristic: The availability heuristic is a mental shortcut that relies on immediate examples that come to mind when evaluating a specific topic, concept, or decision. People tend to overestimate the importance of recent events or vivid examples, which can lead to biased judgments and decision-making.
4. Hindsight Bias: Hindsight bias is the tendency to believe, after an event has occurred, that one would have predicted or expected the outcome beforehand. This bias can lead to overconfidence in one's ability to predict future events and may result in poor decision-making.
5. Overconfidence Bias: Overconfidence bias is the tendency for individuals to overestimate their abilities, skills, or the accuracy of their predictions. This bias can lead to unrealistic expectations, poor decision-making, and increased risk-taking.
6. Fundamental Attribution Error: The fundamental attribution error is the tendency to overemphasize internal characteristics (such as personality traits or abilities) and underestimate external factors when explaining the behavior of others. This can lead to biased judgments about people and their actions.
7. Sunk Cost Fallacy: The sunk cost fallacy occurs when individuals continue to invest time, effort, or resources into a project or decision based on the cumulative prior investment ("sunk costs"), rather than evaluating the current and future value of the investment. This can lead to poor decision-making and an unwillingness to abandon failing projects.
8. Groupthink: Groupthink is a phenomenon that occurs when a group of people, in an effort to avoid conflict and maintain group harmony, reach a consensus without critically examining alternative viewpoints or considering the potential consequences of their decision. This can result in poor decision-making and an inability to recognize potential problems or risks.

Define Affinity Bias and Halo Effect

Affinity Bias: Affinity bias is a type of cognitive bias that causes individuals to prefer those who share similar characteristics, interests, or backgrounds. This bias can manifest in various aspects of life, including professional settings, where people may unconsciously favor colleagues or job candidates who have traits or interests similar to their own. Affinity bias can lead to a lack of diversity and inclusiveness in the workplace and may result in less qualified individuals being chosen for roles or responsibilities.

Halo Effect: The halo effect is a cognitive bias in which an individual's overall impression of a person influences their perception of that person's specific traits or abilities. For example, if someone is perceived as attractive, intelligent, or successful, others may unconsciously attribute other positive qualities to them, such as being a good communicator or leader. The halo effect can impact decision-making in various contexts, including hiring and promotions, and may lead to biased judgments about a person's abilities or performance.

Write definitions of these biases

1. Illusory Superiority: Illusory superiority is a cognitive bias that leads people to overestimate their abilities or positive qualities compared to others. This bias can result in unrealistic self-assessment and hinder personal growth or learning.
2. Projection Bias: Projection bias is the tendency to assume that others share the same beliefs, values, or preferences as oneself. This cognitive bias can lead to misunderstandings and misinterpretations in interpersonal interactions.
3. Recency Bias: Recency bias is the tendency to give greater importance to the most recent events or information, often at the expense of ignoring older, equally relevant data. This bias can negatively impact decision-making and judgments.
4. Salience Bias: Salience bias is the tendency to focus on the most prominent or emotionally striking aspects of a situation, while overlooking less noticeable but potentially more important details. This bias can lead to skewed judgments and decision-making.
5. Selective Perception: Selective perception is a cognitive bias that causes people to filter information based on their pre-existing beliefs, expectations, or preferences. This can result in a distorted understanding of situations, as individuals focus on information that confirms their beliefs and disregard contradictory evidence.
6. Stereotyping: Stereotyping is a cognitive bias that involves forming generalized beliefs or expectations about individuals based on their membership in a specific social group. Stereotypes can lead to prejudiced attitudes and discriminatory behavior.
7. Survivorship Bias: Survivorship bias is the tendency to focus on the successful outcomes or survivors in a particular situation, while ignoring those who failed or did not survive. This cognitive bias can lead to an overestimation of the likelihood of success and an inaccurate understanding of the factors contributing to success.
8. Belief Bias: Belief bias is the tendency to judge the strength of an argument based on the believability of its conclusion, rather than on the quality of the evidence or logic presented. This cognitive bias can result in flawed decision-making and reasoning.
9. Curse of Knowledge: The curse of knowledge is a cognitive bias that occurs when individuals with extensive knowledge on a subject have difficulty considering or communicating with others who possess less knowledge. This bias can lead to misunderstandings and poor communication.
10. Ostrich Effect: The ostrich effect is a cognitive bias that involves avoiding or ignoring negative information or situations in the hope that they will resolve themselves or disappear. This bias can lead to poor decision-making and a failure to address important issues.

Negativity Bias: The tendency to give greater weight to negative experiences or information compared to positive ones. This bias can impact decision-making, memory, and overall perception of events.

Optimism Bias: The tendency to overestimate the likelihood of positive outcomes while underestimating the likelihood of negative outcomes. This cognitive bias can result in unrealistic expectations and poor decision-making.

Dunning-Kruger Effect: A cognitive bias where people with limited knowledge or expertise in a given area overestimate their abilities, while those with more knowledge or expertise tend to underestimate their abilities.

In-group Bias: The tendency to favor members of one's own group, while being more critical or dismissive of those who belong to different groups. This bias can contribute to prejudice and discrimination.

Out-group Homogeneity Bias: The tendency to perceive members of other groups as more similar to each other than they actually are, often leading to stereotyping and discrimination.

False Consensus Effect: The cognitive bias that leads individuals to overestimate the extent to which others share their beliefs, opinions, or preferences.

Just-World Hypothesis: The belief that the world is fundamentally fair, and that people generally get what they deserve. This cognitive bias can lead to victim-blaming and a lack of empathy for those who experience misfortune.

Planning Fallacy: The tendency to underestimate the amount of time or resources needed to complete a task, often leading to overly optimistic predictions and time management issues.

Representativeness Heuristic: A mental shortcut used to judge the likelihood of an event based on how similar it is to a typical or prototypical example, rather than using actual statistical probabilities.

Gambler's Fallacy: The belief that past outcomes in a random process will influence future outcomes, such as believing that a coin toss is "due" for a certain result after a series of opposite results.

Actor-Observer Bias: The tendency to attribute our own actions to situational factors, while attributing others' actions to their personal characteristics.

Authority Bias: The tendency to be more influenced by and trusting of information or opinions provided by perceived authority figures, even if the information is not accurate or reliable.

Bandwagon Effect: The tendency to adopt beliefs, opinions, or behaviors based on the popularity of those beliefs or behaviors, rather than critically evaluating their merits.

Choice-Supportive Bias: The tendency to remember and view one's past choices more positively than they might have been at the time, often to reduce cognitive dissonance and justify the decision.

Illusion of Control: The belief that one has more control over events or outcomes than is actually the case, often leading to overconfidence in one's abilities to influence outcomes.

Mere Exposure Effect: The phenomenon in which people tend to develop a preference for things merely because they are familiar with them, regardless of the objective merits of those things.

Status Quo Bias: The tendency to prefer maintaining the current state of affairs or resisting change, even if change might bring about improvements or benefits.

Endowment Effect: The cognitive bias that causes people to place a higher value on items they own or possess, compared to similar items they do not own.

Peak-End Rule: The tendency to judge experiences based on the most intense (peak) moments and the final moments (end), rather than evaluating the experience as a whole.

Description: Our recent webinar on unconscious biases in the IT workplace provided valuable insights into how cognitive biases can impact decision-making and performance in the IT industry. We explored various biases, their real-life implications, and effective strategies for overcoming them.

Definition of Cognitive Bias: A cognitive bias is a systematic pattern of deviation from rational judgment or objective standards, which occurs due to the way our cognitive system processes information. These biases can influence our thoughts, behaviors, and decision-making processes in both personal and professional settings.

Examples of Cognitive Biases:

* Confirmation Bias: The tendency to search for or interpret information in a way that confirms one's pre-existing beliefs.
* Anchoring Bias: The tendency to rely too heavily on the first piece of information encountered when making decisions.
* Hindsight Bias: The tendency to believe, after an event has occurred, that one would have predicted or expected the outcome beforehand.

Strategies to Overcome Biases:

1. Increase self-awareness and recognize your own biases.
2. Seek diverse perspectives and encourage open communication.
3. Make data-driven decisions and question assumptions.
4. Foster an environment where constructive feedback is valued.
5. Continuously learn and adapt to new information.

Lectures to Develop Knowledge:

1. "Thinking, Fast and Slow" by Daniel Kahneman
2. "Blindspot: Hidden Biases of Good People" by Mahzarin R. Banaji and Anthony G. Greenwald
3. "The Art of Thinking Clearly" by Rolf Dobelli

TED Presentations to Watch:

1. "The Hidden Influence of Social Networks" by Nicholas Christakis
2. "The Surprising Science of Happiness" by Dan Gilbert
3. "How to Make Better Decisions" by Samantha Agoos

"Thinking, Fast and Slow" by Daniel Kahneman:

1. "Nothing in life is as important as you think it is, while you are thinking about it." - The focusing illusion can lead us to overestimate the importance of certain factors in our decision-making.
2. "A reliable way to make people believe in falsehoods is frequent repetition, because familiarity is not easily distinguished from truth." - Familiarity can create cognitive biases and lead to irrational decision-making.
3. "We can be blind to the obvious, and we are also blind to our blindness." - Our cognitive biases can limit our ability to recognize our own shortcomings and errors.
4. "The confidence that individuals have in their beliefs depends mostly on the quality of the story they can tell about what they see, even if they see little." - Overconfidence can arise from our ability to construct convincing narratives, rather than from objective evidence.
5. "The illusion that we understand the past fosters overconfidence in our ability to predict the future." - Hindsight bias can lead to overconfidence in our predictive abilities.

"Blindspot: Hidden Biases of Good People" by Mahzarin R. Banaji and Anthony G. Greenwald:

1. "Most of us believe that we are ethical and unbiased. We imagine we're good decision makers, able to objectively size up a job candidate or a venture deal and reach a fair and rational conclusion that's in our, and our organization's, best interests." - Many people underestimate the influence of cognitive biases on their decision-making.
2. "Hidden biases are surprisingly pervasive, and they can be found even in individuals who genuinely abhor prejudice and discrimination." - Unconscious biases can affect even those who consciously strive for fairness and equality.
3. "Mere awareness of the existence of unconscious prejudice is not sufficient to counteract its effects." - Recognizing biases is important, but more proactive strategies are needed to overcome them.
4. "Creating opportunities for members of different groups to work together as equals can help to break down stereotypes and promote understanding." - Encouraging collaboration and diversity can help reduce the impact of biases.
5. "Even when people are motivated to be fair and impartial, their judgments can still be influenced by hidden biases." - Implicit biases can affect our decision-making even when we are consciously trying to be fair.

"The Art of Thinking Clearly" by Rolf Dobelli:

1. "Cognitive biases make our judgments irrational. They are systematic deviations from logic — from optimal, rational, reasonable thought and behavior." - Cognitive biases can lead to irrational thought patterns and behaviors.
2. "The availability bias causes us to overestimate the importance of information that is easily accessible." - The availability heuristic can lead us to place undue weight on easily accessible information.
3. "The sunk cost fallacy is most dangerous when we have invested a lot of time, money, energy, or love in something. 4. "The more people who follow a certain idea, the better (truer) we deem the idea to be." - The bandwagon effect can lead us to adopt popular beliefs or opinions, even if they are not based on sound reasoning.

Title: CBD Oil vs. CBD Gummies: Which One is Right for You?

Introduction

As the popularity of CBD continues to grow, so does the variety of products available. Two of the most popular CBD products on the market are CBD oil and CBD gummies. Both offer the therapeutic benefits of cannabidiol, but they differ in terms of consumption method, onset of effects, and personal preference. In this article, we will compare CBD oil and CBD gummies to help you decide which one is right for you.

1. Consumption Method

One of the main differences between CBD oil and CBD gummies is the way they are consumed. CBD oil is typically taken sublingually (under the tongue) or added to food and beverages. When taken sublingually, the oil is absorbed directly into the bloodstream through the mucous membranes, allowing for quicker absorption and onset of effects. On the other hand, CBD gummies are chewed and swallowed, making them more like traditional edibles. They must pass through the digestive system before being absorbed into the bloodstream, which can take longer to produce effects.

1. Onset of Effects

Due to the differences in consumption methods, the onset of effects for CBD oil and CBD gummies can vary. CBD oil, when taken sublingually, generally produces effects within 15-45 minutes, while CBD gummies can take anywhere from 30 minutes to 2 hours to take effect. If you are looking for fast-acting relief, CBD oil may be a better choice. However, if you prefer a more gradual and long-lasting effect, CBD gummies might be the way to go.

1. Taste and Discretion

Taste and discretion are important factors for many people when choosing a CBD product. CBD oil often has a distinct earthy taste, which some people find unappealing. However, flavored CBD oils are available for those who want to mask the taste. CBD gummies, on the other hand, come in a variety of flavors and can be easily mistaken for regular candy, making them a more discreet and enjoyable option for those who dislike the taste of CBD oil.

1. Dosage and Consistency

Both CBD oil and CBD gummies provide flexibility when it comes to dosage. CBD oil often comes with a dropper, allowing you to measure out your desired dose easily. You can also increase or decrease the dosage as needed. With CBD gummies, each gummy typically contains a pre-measured amount of CBD, making it easy to track your intake. However, adjusting the dosage may require cutting a gummy in half or taking multiple gummies, depending on the desired amount.

1. Shelf Life and Portability

CBD gummies generally have a longer shelf life compared to CBD oil, as they are less susceptible to oxidation and degradation. They are also more portable, as they can be carried in a bag or pocket without the risk of leakage. CBD oil, on the other hand, should be stored in a cool, dark place to maintain its quality and may not be as convenient to transport.

Conclusion

Ultimately, the choice between CBD oil and CBD gummies comes down to personal preference and your specific needs. If you're looking for fast-acting relief, prefer a customizable dosage, and don't mind the earthy taste, CBD oil might be the best option for you. On the other hand, if you want a more discreet, enjoyable, and portable option with a longer shelf life, CBD gummies could be the way to go.

Always consult with a healthcare professional before incorporating CBD into your wellness routine, and choose high-quality, reputable products to ensure safety and efficacy. By understanding the differences between CBD oil and CBD gummies, you can make an informed decision that suits your needs and preferences.

Title: The Science Behind CBD: How It Really Works in the Body

Introduction

Cannabidiol, or CBD, has become increasingly popular in recent years due to its potential health benefits and non-psychoactive nature. While many people have experienced the positive effects of CBD, the underlying science behind how it works in the body may not be as well known. In this article, we will explore the science behind CBD, shedding light on its interaction with the human body and how it produces its therapeutic effects.

1. The Endocannabinoid System

To understand how CBD works, it's essential to first understand the endocannabinoid system (ECS). The ECS is a complex cell-signaling system found in all mammals, responsible for maintaining balance and regulating various physiological processes, including mood, pain, inflammation, and sleep. The ECS is composed of three main components: endocannabinoids, receptors, and enzymes.

Endocannabinoids are naturally occurring compounds that resemble the active compounds found in cannabis, such as CBD and THC. The two primary endocannabinoids are anandamide and 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG). These molecules bind to cannabinoid receptors found throughout the body, triggering various responses.

There are two main types of cannabinoid receptors: CB1 and CB2. CB1 receptors are primarily found in the brain and central nervous system, while CB2 receptors are located in the immune system and peripheral tissues. When endocannabinoids bind to these receptors, they help regulate essential bodily functions and maintain homeostasis.

Finally, enzymes in the ECS break down endocannabinoids once they have fulfilled their purpose. The two main enzymes are fatty acid amide hydrolase (FAAH), which breaks down anandamide, and monoacylglycerol lipase (MAGL), which degrades 2-AG.

1. How CBD Interacts with the ECS

Unlike THC, which binds directly to CB1 receptors and produces psychoactive effects, CBD has a more complex and indirect interaction with the ECS. CBD does not bind strongly to either CB1 or CB2 receptors. Instead, it appears to modulate the activity of these receptors by influencing the way they interact with other cannabinoids and endocannabinoids.

One of CBD's primary effects is its ability to increase levels of anandamide in the body. It does this by inhibiting the FAAH enzyme, which is responsible for breaking down anandamide. Higher levels of anandamide can lead to enhanced mood, reduced pain, and other therapeutic effects.

1. CBD's Interaction with Other Receptors

CBD's effects are not limited to its interaction with the ECS. It also interacts with various non-cannabinoid receptors, contributing to its diverse range of benefits. Some of these interactions include:

* Serotonin Receptors: CBD can bind to 5-HT1A serotonin receptors, which play a role in mood regulation, anxiety, and pain perception. This interaction may explain CBD's potential in treating anxiety and depression.
* Vanilloid Receptors: CBD can activate TRPV1 (vanilloid) receptors, which are responsible for mediating pain, inflammation, and body temperature. This may contribute to CBD's analgesic and anti-inflammatory effects.
* GPR55 Receptors: CBD has been shown to block GPR55 receptors, which can modulate blood pressure, bone density, and inflammation. This interaction may contribute to CBD's potential cardiovascular and bone health benefits.

Conclusion

The science behind CBD is complex and still being unraveled. However, it's clear that CBD's interaction with the endocannabinoid system and other receptors plays a crucial role in its therapeutic potential. As research continues to advance, our understanding of how CBD works in the body will

Title: Demystifying CBD: Common Myths and Misconceptions Debunked

Introduction

However, with this growing interest come many myths and misconceptions surrounding CBD and its effects. In this article, we will debunk some common myths and clarify the facts about CBD, helping you make informed decisions about its use.

1. Myth: CBD Gets You High

Fact: CBD is a non-psychoactive compound found in the cannabis plant, meaning it does not produce the "high" typically associated with marijuana. The psychoactive effects of cannabis are primarily caused by tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), another compound in the plant. CBD products sold legally contain only trace amounts of THC (typically less than 0.3%), which is not enough to produce psychoactive effects.

1. Myth: CBD Is Only Derived from Marijuana

Fact: CBD can be extracted from both marijuana and hemp plants, which are both members of the cannabis family. However, hemp-derived CBD is more prevalent in the market due to its lower THC content, which meets legal requirements. Hemp-derived CBD products are federally legal in the United States, whereas marijuana-derived CBD products are only legal in states with medical or recreational marijuana laws.

1. Myth: CBD Is a Miracle Cure-All

Fact: While CBD has shown promise in treating various health conditions, it is not a miracle cure-all. CBD has been found to have potential benefits for pain relief, anxiety, sleep, and inflammation, among others, but more research is needed to fully understand its effects and establish optimal dosages. Title: Debunking Common CBD Myths: Separating Fact from Fiction

Introduction

In this article, we will debunk some of the most common CBD myths and provide accurate, evidence-based information to help you make informed decisions about CBD use.

1. Myth: CBD Will Get You High

Fact: CBD is a non-psychoactive compound found in the cannabis plant, meaning it does not produce the intoxicating effects or "high" associated with THC, the primary psychoactive component of marijuana. CBD products derived from hemp contain less than 0.3% THC, which is not enough to cause any psychoactive effects. 1. Myth: All CBD Products Are the Same

Fact: There is a wide range of CBD products available on the market, and not all are created equal. The quality, potency, and purity of CBD products can vary significantly depending on factors such as the extraction method, the source of the hemp, and the manufacturing process. It's crucial to choose reputable, transparent brands that provide third-party lab test results to ensure you're getting a safe, high-quality product.

1. Myth: CBD is Addictive

Fact: According to the World Health Organization (WHO), CBD has a good safety profile and is not associated with the risk of addiction or dependence. Unlike some prescription medications and opioids, CBD is not considered habit-forming and has not been shown to lead to substance abuse or withdrawal symptoms.

1. Myth: Higher Doses of CBD Are Always Better

Fact: CBD does not have a one-size-fits-all dosage, and more is not always better. 1. Myth: CBD is a Cure-All

Conclusion

Title: The Science of CBD: Exploring the Endocannabinoid System and How CBD Works

Introduction

CBD, or cannabidiol, has gained widespread attention for its potential therapeutic benefits. To fully understand how CBD works within the body, it's essential to explore the endocannabinoid system (ECS), a complex cell-signaling system that plays a crucial role in regulating various physiological processes. In this article, we will delve into the ECS, its components, and the mechanisms through which CBD interacts with this system to produce its potential effects.

1. Understanding the Endocannabinoid System (ECS)

The ECS is a cell-signaling system present throughout the body, involved in regulating numerous physiological processes, such as mood, pain, appetite, sleep, and immune function. The ECS is composed of three main components:

* Endocannabinoids: These are naturally occurring compounds in the body that are structurally similar to cannabinoids found in cannabis plants. The two primary endocannabinoids are anandamide (AEA) and 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG).
* Receptors: Endocannabinoids bind to specific receptors on cell surfaces, triggering various responses within the body. The two primary types of receptors are CB1 receptors (mainly found in the brain and central nervous system) and CB2 receptors (primarily located in the immune system and peripheral tissues).
* Enzymes: These are responsible for breaking down endocannabinoids once they have fulfilled their function. The two primary enzymes are fatty acid amide hydrolase (FAAH), which breaks down AEA, and monoacylglycerol lipase (MAGL), which degrades 2-AG.
1. How CBD Interacts with the ECS

Unlike THC, the psychoactive compound in cannabis, CBD does not directly bind to CB1 or CB2 receptors. Instead, it is believed to exert its potential effects through indirect mechanisms, such as:

* Inhibition of endocannabinoid breakdown: CBD may inhibit the activity of enzymes responsible for breaking down endocannabinoids like AEA, thereby increasing their levels and prolonging their effects.
* Modulation of receptor activity: CBD may act as an allosteric modulator, altering the shape of CB1 receptors and influencing their ability to bind with endocannabinoids. This can result in a dampening of the receptor's activity, potentially reducing the psychoactive effects of THC.
* Interaction with non-ECS receptors: CBD may also interact with various non-ECS receptors, such as serotonin (5-HT1A) receptors, which are involved in mood regulation, and transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) receptors, which play a role in pain perception.
1. CBD's Potential Therapeutic Effects

The complex interaction of CBD with the ECS and non-ECS receptors may contribute to its potential therapeutic effects, such as:

* Anti-inflammatory: CBD's potential to reduce inflammation may be partly attributed to its interaction with CB2 receptors and its ability to influence immune system function.
* Analgesic: CBD's potential pain-relieving properties may be due to its interaction with TRPV1 receptors and modulation of the ECS, which plays a key role in pain regulation.
* Anxiolytic: CBD's potential anxiety-reducing effects may be linked to its interaction with 5-HT1A receptors, which are involved in serotonin regulation and mood balance.

Conclusion

The endocannabinoid system plays a vital role in maintaining overall health and well-being. CBD's complex interaction with the ECS and non-ECS receptors may contribute to its potential therapeutic effects on various physiological processes. As research on CBD and the ECS continues to advance, our understanding of the mechanisms behind CBD's potential benefits will continue to grow

Title: CBD and Drug Interactions: What You Need to Know Before Mixing CBD with Medications

Introduction

As CBD's popularity continues to rise, it's essential to be aware of its potential interactions with medications. While CBD is generally considered safe and well-tolerated, it can interact with certain drugs, potentially impacting their effectiveness or causing adverse effects. In this article, we'll explore how CBD may interact with medications, discuss specific drug interactions, and offer guidance on safely incorporating CBD into your wellness routine while taking medications.

1. CBD and the Cytochrome P450 System

One of the primary ways CBD interacts with medications is through the cytochrome P450 (CYP450) enzyme system. This system, located in the liver, is responsible for metabolizing a wide range of drugs. CBD can inhibit certain CYP450 enzymes, such as CYP3A4, which may alter the way the body processes some medications. This can lead to increased or decreased levels of the drug in the bloodstream, potentially causing adverse effects or reducing the drug's effectiveness.

1. Specific Drug Interactions

While not an exhaustive list, the following are some examples of medications that may interact with CBD:

* Blood thinners: CBD can potentially increase the blood-thinning effects of medications like warfarin, which may increase the risk of bleeding.
* Benzodiazepines: CBD may enhance the sedative effects of benzodiazepines, such as diazepam, potentially increasing drowsiness and the risk of central nervous system depression.
* Antidepressants: CBD's potential interaction with certain antidepressants, like fluoxetine, may lead to increased levels of the drug in the bloodstream, potentially resulting in adverse effects.
* Antiepileptic drugs: CBD may interact with antiepileptic medications like clobazam, potentially increasing the risk of side effects such as drowsiness and sedation.
* Beta-blockers: CBD's potential interaction with beta-blockers, like metoprolol, may increase the risk of low blood pressure and slow heart rate.
1. Tips for Safely Using CBD with Medications

If you're considering using CBD while taking medications, follow these tips to ensure your safety:

* Consult with a healthcare professional: Before starting CBD, discuss your plans with a healthcare professional, particularly if you're taking prescription medications. They can help determine if CBD is appropriate for you and provide guidance on dosage and potential drug interactions.
* Start with a low dose: Begin with a small dose of CBD and gradually increase as needed, under the guidance of your healthcare professional. This may help minimize the risk of adverse effects and potential drug interactions.
* Monitor for side effects: Pay close attention to any changes in your body or the effectiveness of your medications after starting CBD. Report any side effects or concerns to your healthcare professional immediately.

Conclusion

While CBD has potential therapeutic benefits, it's essential to be aware of its potential interactions with medications. By consulting with a healthcare professional, starting with a low dose, and closely monitoring for side effects, you can minimize the risk of adverse effects and drug interactions while incorporating CBD into your wellness routine. Always prioritize safety and take necessary precautions when combining CBD with medications.

- Increase engagement on Twitter and Discord
- Promote Crystale to the target audience
- Create a referral program for existing members to invite their friends to join the Discord and follow on Twitter
- Post regularly on Discord with updates and teasers about the game's development and upcoming features.
- Share exclusive content from influencers, such as gameplay previews, cosplays, and artwork.

• Summon or Sacrifice 1 Servant;
• Use Spell Crystals (No maximum usage if MP is sufficient);
• Move every unit one adjacent tile;

8. CrystalE Economics
Creating a game economy is one thing, however, creating a sustainable game tokenomy is
another thing altogether. The key takeaway, which is also one of our fundamental pillars, is that
the community must have fun and remain protected from malicious intent at all times. We also
believe that to create a sustainable economy, data on the participant’s behavior is critical.
Additionally, we strongly believe that during the initial years of Crystale the emphasis should
be on sustainable growth and player experience. We believe that if the economic incentive

(which in this case is a token) is market-driven, the reason for people to play is market-
dependent. In the end, we are a game utilizing blockchain technology. We are not creating NFTs

and Cryptocurrency in a gaming use case.
For those reasons, we’re holding off on the release of a token for the initial years. Another
reason being is that our devised utility for a native token doesn’t necessarily need a token.
Moreover, the risks (speculation, manipulation etc.) regarding a token can be mitigated by using
stablecoins and existing currencies for our in-game utilities. Next to that, research has shown
that money reduces intrinsic motivation (Journal of Economic Perspectives, 2011), which is
crucial to long-term player retention. Introducing a native token could also have negative effects
on migrating web2 gamers to web3 due to too much unfamiliarity.
In order for Crystale to be sustainable, we envision a 70/30 split on all generated revenue. This
means that 70% goes directly to the reserve to be used for operational costs and the community
(p&e rewards, events etc.). The additional 30% will be used for the treasury.
The treasury will serve as the backbone of the community and will be used for innovations in
the Crystale Verse. If ever needed, the treasury will be used in the event of an emergency. Every
quarter, an analysis will be completed in order to assess if any opportunities and/or risk could
occur for the next two upcoming quarters. If the opportunities outweigh the risks, 2.5% to a
maximum of 5% (per year) of the treasury will be used to potentially increase the strength of the backbone

            'Down': (x1, y1 + self.size, x2, y2 + self.size),
